rows.notes: The cited document is a narrative review (bibliographical synthesis) of Partial Root-zone Drying irrigation; it reports no data, experiment, survey or model runs of its own. All statements on water productivity, wetting/salt fronts and root activity are drawn from other studies (e.g. Kriedemann and Goodwin 2003, Abdelraouf and Ragab 2018, Kaman et al. 2006, Slamini et al. 2022, which is a separate paper). Q1 is therefore 'no' and all subsequent questions 'no'. The review does discuss the idea that PRD/drip effectiveness depends on soil type, wetting depth and frequency, and salt accumulation in the root zone, which is consistent with the claim, but only as a synthesis of cited work.

notes: Document is a complete review article (Slamini et al. 2022, Agric. Water Manag. 271:107807) with sections on PRD concept, physiology, WUE, nutrient uptake, pollutant leaching, salinity and citrus applications; no primary data are reported.
